ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper part of the figure is a sulfur-containing central thiocarbonyl structure, in which the central carbon forms a C=S double bond with the upper S and is respectively connected to the left and right two nitrogen-containing five-membered rings; there are curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Below is a diol/R substituent fragment containing two hydroxyl groups, including R, R¹, two carbons, and two O/H labels. Reasoning: Count in blocks according to the specified method, and exclude all bonds involving hydrogen. The left five-membered ring has 5 heavy-atom bonds; the right five-membered ring has 5 heavy-atom bonds. The central thiocarbonyl connection portion includes 2 C-N bonds from the central carbon to the two ring nitrogens, plus 1 C=S bond, for a total of 3 bonds. The lower diol/R fragment includes R-C, C-C, upper C-OH, C-R¹, and lower C-OH, for a total of 5 non-hydrogen bonds. The total is 5 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 18.

method.method_draft: Partition the drawing into fragments. First count the left ring as 5 heavy-atom bonds and the right ring as 5 heavy-atom bonds. Then count the central thiocarbonyl linker: two C-N bonds from the carbonyl carbon to the two ring nitrogens plus the C=S bond, giving 3. Finally count the lower diol/R fragment: R-C, C-C, C-OH at the upper carbon, C-R1, and C-OH at the lower carbon, giving 5. Ignore both curved arrows and all O-H/C-H bonds. Add 5 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 18.
